    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    What all 32 NFL teams should be thankful for this Thanksgiving

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.
    • The gap between the best team and the worst team in the NFL is quite large, but even though not all teams have the playoffs in their future, or even a winning record, they can still be thankful for what they do have,.
    • Thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to plan for every team.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.

    The gap between the best team and the worst team in the NFL is quite large, but even though not all teams have the playoffs in their future, or even a winning record, they can still be thankful for what they do have,.

    Thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to plan for every team. Some franchises enter the holiday firmly in the Super Bowl race, while others are already measuring progress through young players, improved units and the draft capital that could shape a brighter future.

    Winning despite turnovers – The Bills have a lot of reasons for gratitude. This one is somewhat of a good news, bad news situation: the team is turning the ball over more than they should, but they are still getting wins. It just goes to show that great teams will find ways to win games regardless. Josh Allen, James Cook, and their record are the obvious things they should be thankful for, but this one is most interesting to me because, as a team that has turned the ball over twice in three of the last four games and five times in a single game this season, 9-1 is impressive.

    Drake Maye value – The Patriots have had a difficult season in terms of injuries, so much so that they're running out of spots on IR, and on-field struggles even when healthy. Quarterback Drake Maye is out for an extended period of time, likely the rest of the season, and without him the offense fell flat. The team still had their fair share of struggles with Maye, don't get me wrong, but if him being sidelined proved anything, it's how valuable he is to the team. In a season where many were questioning his real impact, wondering if last year was a fluke, the team can be grateful that when they do get Maye back (even if it's next year), the offense will be bumped back up.

    Pass defense – The Jets are another team far outside the playoff race, but it's not all bad! Heading into Week 11, the Jets pass defense was fifth-best in the league, allowing 196.8 yards per game through 10 weeks. This alone won't get them to a Super Bowl, but on a team with many complications to point to, they can be thankful that something is working.

    Recent findings suggest that forcing turnovers – Looking at the Dolphins record, it can be hard to think that they have anything to be thankful for. A high draft pick is one thing they can be grateful for, but so is their defense. They were tied for fifth-most interceptions with nine through 10 weeks and added two more against the Bills last week. The run defense had the challenge of facing Jonathan Taylor, Jahmyr Gibbs and James Cook and held them to under 100 yards each.

    It has been revealed that joe Burrow — Cincinnati boasts a reinvigorated defense (led by Dexter Lawrence) and the best receiving duo in the NFL in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Burrow, however, remains the key to the Bengals' success. He's right now on pace to become the first player in history to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing at least 70% of his passes. He's among the MVP front-runners.

    Todd Monken — With respect to John Harbaugh, Monken should win NFL Coach of the Year if the Browns continue to win. Cleveland is 6-4 and would be in the playoffs if the postseason started today. Monken has revived Deshaun Watson's career.

    Jaylen Warren — Warren was arguably the biggest reason for Pittsburgh's 6-2 start. The former undrafted rookie rushed for over 700 yards over that span that included four 100-yard games. Warren and the Steelers' offense have fallen off in recent weeks, though. Warren becomes even more valuable within the offense as the Aaron Rodgers drama sparked a quarterback change.

    Derrick Henry — While it's been a lost season in Baltimore, Ravens fans still get a chance to watch an all-time great do his thing. Henry is still playing well and setting new milestones in his 11th NFL season. This season, he's moved into third all-time in rushing touchdowns and seventh in career rushing yards.

    Liam Coen – The Jaguars are now 20-7 under coach Liam Coen, who has turned this franchise from an afterthought to a Super Bowl contender. Coen has Trevor Lawrence finally living up to the lofty expectations set before him as a prospect coming out of Clemson, and has put together an impressive staff that includes defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile and offensive coordinator Grant Udinski. Both could be head coaches next year.

    C.J. Stroud – Imagine how disappointing the Texans would be this year if it weren't for the play of C.J. Stroud? He's thrown three touchdowns in three straight games, and scored at least two touchdowns in seven straight games. That's the longest such streak in franchise history. Stroud has thrown 22 touchdowns compared to just four interceptions this season. We no longer have to wonder if the Texans have a franchise quarterback.

    In a recent development, the season is almost over – There are just six games remaining in the regular season. That's good news for Colts fans.

    Recent findings suggest that future drafts – The one-win Titans traded away star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker for some nice draft capital. Tennessee now holds four first-round picks and three second-round picks in the next two drafts, which could expedite a seemingly never-ending rebuild. As long as Mike Borgonzi doesn't draft another developmental pass rusher.

    According to recent reports, patrick Mahomes back on top – The Chiefs are back and so is Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City's woes of last season are over, and the fans can breathe a sigh of relief that last year was a fluke. Mahomes has 22 touchdowns with just four interceptions this year, along with 2,709 yards. He is looking like the Super Bowl contender he has been in the past, and his offense has fixed many of the mistakes they had last season. With Mahomes playing like he is, this team has a real chance of going all the way.

    Division still in reach – Last season the Broncos won the division, but that was with the Chiefs struggling. This year, K.C. is among the top in the league and Denver is still within reach of the divisional title. That is a major accomplishment for Sean Payton's squad.

    Mendoza Era begins – The Raiders season has been filled with ups and downs. It started off strong, but then took a turn. The hope the Raiders and their fans can have is that the Fernando Mendoza era has begun and they can start to get excited about who they anticipate to be their franchise guy.

    High draft pick – The Chargers season hasn't been what they hoped, leaving lots of questions about their quarterback and coach. The good news is that they will be getting a high draft pick this year. Now they just need to do something with it.

    John Harbaugh -- The New York Giants are fresh off a 23-18 win over the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) in Week 11 that has the Giants out to a two-game lead in the NFC East over the Cowboys.

    Upcoming coach John Harbaugh is pushing all the right buttons and has the Giants tracking toward a division title despite Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns suffering season-ending injuries within the first three weeks of the 2026 season. He is certainly someone the Giants are grateful to have leading their football team.

    Recent findings suggest that dak Prescott -- Prescott is dragging his 29th-ranked scoring defense (28.4 points per game allowed) into the NFC East division race by powering the league's No. 4 scoring offense (30.6 points per game). Prescott became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club.

    Prescott now ranks second in the NFL in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25) while ranking eighth in passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21). He is pulling off one of the NFL's biggest carry jobs this season, and he is someone that owner/general manager Jerry Jones should be eternally grateful to have leading his football team.

    According to recent reports, jayden Daniels -- Daniels looks like his 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year self with all of his tools available to him. Daniels finished with 289 passing yards on 23 of 35 attempts while leading the Commanders with 55 yards rushing in a 22-20, buzzer-beating victory over the AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals. Washington now has consecutive wins over two first-place teams, the Giants and Bengals, no less, for the first time since the 2024 season, when Daniels won Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and the Commanders reached the NFC Championship Game.

    After tossing a 32-yard game-winning touchdown to Stefon Diggs to shock the Giants and then the game-winning drive on Monday against the AFC North-leading Bengals, it's clear Daniels has his magic back.

    According to recent reports, saquon Barkley -- The 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back powered the Philadelphia Eagles (75 rushing yards, including a 38-yard rushing touchdown, on 17 carries) to a 19-16 upset victory of the Pittsburgh Steelers to end the franchise's seven-game winning streak. Barkley is at the moment on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career in a lost year for his franchise.

    In a recent development, jahmyr Gibbs -- Gibbs leads the entire NFL in rushing yards (1,098), scrimmage yards (1,502) and touchdowns from scrimmage (15) through the first 11 weeks of the 2026 season. Gibbs is now the first player with 1,500-plus scrimmage yards and 15-plus scrimmage touchdowns through the first 10 games of a season since Emmitt Smith accomplished the feat in 1995.

    Jeffery Simmons -- The Chicago Bears needed a game-changing presence along their defensive line, and All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been just that in his first three games. He racked up 3.0 sacks in Chicago's 21-13 Week 11 win over the Latest Orleans Saints, so Simmons is now up to 5.0 sacks and three consecutive wins in his three-game Bears career. Despite playing just three games with the Bears since coming over in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, he now co-leads his new team in sacks (5.0) with Austin Booker, who has played in all 10 games for Chicago this season. Simmons is now the only player in NFL history with five-plus sacks and three wins in his first three games after switching teams during a season,  according to CBS Sports Research.

    Sources indicate that kirk Cousins -- Yes, the Minnesota Vikings are fresh off being steamrolled 35-10 on "Sunday Night Football" against the top-seeded San Francisco 49ers (9-1), but Kirk Cousins stabilizes their offense in a way Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz could not. He helped lead them to a 30-10 victory at the Green Bay Packers in Week 10 by doing just enough. Minnesota is in the NFC North division title race going forward because Cousins is a Viking once again.

    Jordan Love -- Yes, the Green Bay Packers' patchwork offensive line didn't give Jordan Love (220 yards passing, one touchdown, one interception on 17-of-27 passing) a chance against Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense in Week 10 in a 30-10 defeat at Lambeau Field. He was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a single game this season with Deshaun Watson (twice) and Justin Herbert. Love made some strong throws when he had the time.

    According to recent reports, A weak division – There has been no greater beneficiary of the NFC South's ineptitude since the start of 2025 than the Panthers. They won the division with a losing record last season and -- with their first-place standing at just 5-5 -- are on track to do so again in 2026.

    Industry observers note that defensive improvement – For all the love the Vikings and Seahawks receive for their vicious defenses, it is actually the Buccaneers who lead the NFL in EPA per play allowed. Tampa Bay's unit has only gotten better as the season progresses and is on a new level right now, having forced at least four turnovers in each of the last three games. It also completed the only shutout of the season in Week 8.

    Recent findings suggest that three optimism-inspiring wins – The losses have been bad. There is no way around that. But conversely, each of Atlanta's three wins is as stellar as the losses are concerning. The Falcons handed the Packers their worst loss of the year. They demolished the Saints for their only divisional victory. And they are responsible for the only blemish on the 49ers' resume. The lows might be low, but the highs prove that Atlanta can hang with anyone.

    Industry observers note that jordyn Tyson's arrival from injured reserve – After he spent the first eight weeks of his career on IR, the No. 8 overall pick displayed all kinds of promise in two healthy games. He racked up 11 catches on 13 targets in his second outing, which is a massive workload for a rookie with only eight quarters of experience and one that suggests he could carry this offense if he stays in the lineup over the next month and a half.

    Sources indicate that brock Purdy's career year – It will be difficult to outpace Joe Burrow in the MVP race, but Purdy is in the conversation. He was the catalyst behind the 49ers' stupendous first half of the season and is now the NFL's all-time leader in career passer rating, success rate and adjusted yards per attempt. Not bad for a former Mr. Irrelevant. Most impressive is that he is playing his best football while dealing with a plethora of injuries at wide receiver.

    According to recent reports, quarterback depth – That Mike Macdonald had to assert that Sam Darnold is the team's starter when healthy is a testament more to Drew Lock playing up than Darnold playing down. Lock is 3-0 as a starter and won the season opener after taking over in the first quarter. To have someone capable of not only keeping the offense afloat when the starter is hurt but to thrive with a 125.6 passer rating is a major reason why Seattle is still in the postseason hunt.

    Strength of schedule regression – If not for the highly manageable slate the Rams faced from Weeks 7-10, the conversation around Los Angeles would reek even more of disappointment than it already does. The combined records of the last four teams they played: 11-26-1. That was strong medicine for a preseason Super Bowl favorite that stunningly opened the year at 2-4.

    Trey McBride – At least the Cardinals have a building block to construct a foundation around as they embark on their rebuild. Since Jeremiyah Love's rookie year has been a complete injury-riddled disappointment and the wide receiver group is torn down to the studs, it is a good thing McBride is around to provide some semblance of life on a team whose season is headed down the drain.

    Recent findings suggest that aaron Rodgers' recent comments about Mike McCarthy have drawn the ire of some of his former Green Bay Packers teammates. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang and former Packers receivers James Jones and Greg Jennings have publicly denounced Rodgers' treatment of McCarthy while taking their former coach's side following a chaotic 48-hour period in Pittsburgh.

    In a recent development, rodgers scorched McCarthy on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, accusing his now-former coach of falling asleep at meetings, being late or absent from other meetings, not watching film in a timely manner and not developing a rapport with some of his players, especially the team's defensive players. Rodgers was benched after giving McCarthy an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. McCarthy benched Rodgers, and the Steelers released him after Rodgers publicly criticized McCarthy.

    "I think it's despicable," Lang said on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it.".

    Lang, who spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, said that he is in a group chat with several former Packers who share his sentiment on the situation.

    "I think it's just completely unnecessary," he noted. "I think it's victim mentality.".

    TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/0oiS3PybCn.

    Jones, who also spent eight seasons with Rodgers and McCarthy in Green Bay, remarked he, too, is in a group text with former Packers teammates who don't agree with Rodgers' handling of McCarthy.

    "How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones stated on the Speakeasy podcast. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike.".

    Jennings, who spent seven seasons in Green Bay and caught two touchdowns in the Packers' Super Bowl win over the Steelers, called Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy "distasteful." Jennings also criticized Rodgers for putting his former teammates in Pittsburgh in an awkward situation.

    "If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings said on "First Thing First." "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything.".

    According to recent reports, @GregJennings weighs in on Steelers releasing former teammate Aaron Rodgers:“It was very distasteful… If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don’t do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers... They are playing for something.” pic.twitter.com/whPyBO7K2p.

    The general consensus among Rodgers' former Packers teammates is that Rodgers should have handled the situation behind closed doors, even if some of his accusations about McCarthy are true.

    It has been revealed that "I don't even care if it's the truth," Jones said. "Have the conversation with Mike in there. This is not something you go to the media bashing somebody. I would not do this to people that I love.".

That's exactly what the Boston Bruins have done as they've stood out for the right reasons in a deep Atlantic Division.

    Boston currently leads the division with 15 points, and while the Tampa Bay Lightning's record is technically better, the Bruins' plus-14 goal differential is tied for second in the NHL.

    Industry observers note that the biggest reason for this fast start has been the play of Jeremy Swayman in goal. He's allowed one or fewer goals in half of his starts, and Swayman's 8.02 goals saved above average ranks second to old Beantown running mate Linus Ullmark, per Natural Stat Trick.

    We have a long way to go before we start discussing Vezina Trophy candidates seriously, but Swayman certainly has the potential to carry Boston to the postseason.

    It helps that David Pastrnak is an elite playmaker, and the Bruins have been getting contributions from young forwards Fraser Minten and James Hagens. Morgan Geekie has also gone from goal-scoring machine to distributor with seven assists in 10 games.

    The Atlantic Division will be a heavyweight brawl throughout the season, but to this point, the Bruins have proven to be a worthy combatant. With that in mind, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    According to recent reports, it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.

    According to recent reports, then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.

    Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:.

    It has been revealed that "I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how important it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run.".

    Matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.

    Sources indicate that after a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.

    Teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers.

    It's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose.

    Industry observers note that larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.

    In a recent development, things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable.

    According to recent reports, lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an important consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.

    Recent findings suggest that the Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked.

    Recent findings suggest that the Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027.

    Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:.

    Morris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.

    In a recent development, clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend big dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.

    Recent findings suggest that the Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is vital and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.

    Sources indicate that more outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:.

    Rodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line?

    • According to recent reports, did Wemby just...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    According to recent reports, let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    According to recent reports, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    According to recent reports, officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    According to recent reports, that begs an important question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    Wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    According to recent reports, fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no intends to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he said after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

    The Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has confirmed the trade.

    Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

    In a recent development, the Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the major leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

    Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control issues since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

    Sources indicate that espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

    Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

    Sources indicate that at worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

    Espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

    It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

    It's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

    Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

    The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

    Tech Report: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Recent findings suggest that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Fresh Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He noted at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Recent findings suggest that hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Newly introduced Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a newly introduced era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Goaltending has been an issue in Latest Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    Recent findings suggest that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Fresh Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    It has been revealed that in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    Sources indicate that the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Industry observers note that although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Upcoming Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    It has been revealed that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Fresh Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    According to recent reports, let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Recent findings suggest that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    According to recent reports, if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    Sources indicate that the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Steelers president Art Rooney II spent part of his Thanksgiving addressing his team's decision to bench, then release Aaron Rodgers following his actions with Mike McCarthy. McCarthy benched Rodgers after Rodgers gave him an ultimatum: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. The Steelers released Rodgers after he went scorched earth on McCarthy during a 35-minute interview on "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    "I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that.".

    Rooney took glitch with Rodgers' decision to publicly air his grievances with McCarthy, especially with the Steelers just days away from playing a significant game against the Denver Broncos.

    "There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney stated. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure.".

    Perhaps the most interesting thing Rooney said was regarding Pittsburgh's play-calling.

    Industry observers note that "The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had," Rooney said. "Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn't working.".

    Industry observers note that one possible example of this may have been late in the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 8 win over the Browns. The Steelers were running at will, which made Pittsburgh's decision to call three straight passing plays inside Cleveland's 10-yard-line a head scratching decision to say the least. McCarthy accepted blame for those play calls when asked about them afterward.

    In a recent development, regarding his team's future, Rooney said he is optimistic that Mason Rudolph can lead the Steelers' offense. Rudolph, a nine-year veteran who has 20 career starts under his belt, delivered for the Steelers when he was in a similar spot in 2023.

    When asked if he regrets his decision to bring Rodgers back, Rooney said he was disappointed with how things turned out.

    According to recent reports, "We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll," he said. "We had high expectations.

    "It's easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn't expecting it to go this way this year.".

    Damian Lillard stars in his Milwaukee return in another stark reminder of how bleak things are for the Bucks

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up!
    • Bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores.
    • Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

    Bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

    Lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

    According to recent reports, trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he said, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

    Industry observers note that lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard said.

    No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

    In a recent development, "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori stated pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

    The moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

    The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

    According to recent reports, "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard noted Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

    The desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

    Five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

    And the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

    No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

    Just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a new promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

The new extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.

    Recent findings suggest that melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year.
    • And then there's been everything in between.
    • So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year. The Grizzlies were a popular pick to surprise some folks this year, but nobody saw this coming. On the other hand, Luka Dončić and Victor Wembanyama are lording over the league like castles on a hill, and that wasn't so hard to predict.

    And then there's been everything in between. All the injuries, perhaps most notably. The Raptors and Pacers entered the season being hyped as fresh-look contenders, but so far Tyrese Haliburton and Kawhi Leonard have combined to play six games. The Warriors went from an eight-game winning streak to the Washington Generals with one Stephen Curry abdominal tweak. The 76ers can't lose a clutch game in a maze. Paul George has been reborn in Boston. The Rockets are flying. The Heat are getting hot. The Knicks' fog is lifting. It feels like Damian Lillard never left the Blazers. This rookie class looks potentially historic.

    So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware. Who's been the MVP so far? What about the best rookie? What has been the biggest surprise? Biggest disappointment? In light of what we've seen so far, is anyone ready to change their preseason Finals pick? Our staff took a collective shot at tackling these topics below.

    Botkin: It's a two-horse race so far and nobody is going to argue much with either pick, but I'm going with Luka. I thought the Lakers would be good (their over/under 46.5 win total was way too low), but not tied-for-the-best-record-in-the-league good. Likewise, we all knew Luka would score huge, but not damn-near 40 PPG huge. Throw in north of seven assists and seven rebounds and almost two steals a night, and the numbers are simply too overwhelming to deny.

    Gonzalez: This is really tough. Luka Dončić has been playing some of the best basketball of his career, and he's a huge reason why the Lakers are down as my big surprise over the first month of the season. But for as good as Luka has been, Wemby's two-way dominance gives him the edge here. Wembanyama had the second 50-point game of his career against the Mavs, and he's averaging a 28-point double-double on 53% shooting from the field. He's also blocking an outrageous 4.1 shots per game and averaging more than a steal per outing. There's no answer for him at either end of the floor.

    According to recent reports, kalland: Wemby's been awesome but for the first month it's gotta be Luka. He's averaging 38 points per game on 47/38/86 splits! The Lakers are 13-3 in spite of defensive concerns, and it's because Dončić is out of his mind. What's amazing is he's going to have to keep up this ridiculous pace to win MVP and for the Lakers to remain at the top of the West. I'm excited to see how long he can maintain this level.

    Maloney: I won't argue with anyone who picks Luka Dončić when he's averaging nearly 40 points per game, but I'm going with Wembanyama because of his two-way dominance. He's third in scoring, fourth in rebounding and first in blocks by a significant margin. The 1.7 blocks-per-game gap between Wembanyama (3.9) and Donovan Clingan (2.2), who sits in second, is as significant as the gap between Clingan and Dean Wade (0.5), who ranks 102nd in the league. In 483 minutes with Wembanyama on the floor this season, the Spurs have a 98.7 defensive rating; in 290 minutes without him, they have a 123.4 defensive rating. Overall, Wembanyama has an unfathomable +41.5 net rating differential.

    According to recent reports, quinn: Dončić is flirting with 40 points per game. He's leading the NBA in both 3-point attempts and free throws. He's the undisputed engine of the NBA's best offense, one that dies whenever he rests. The Lakers have the NBA's best record because Luka Dončić is on their team. That's it. They're average at basically everything else: rebounding, defense, you name it. But their offense dominates because he is on their team. Victor Wembanyama has much more to work with around him. No one else is even in their galaxy, though Stephen Curry might've had a case had he stayed healthy.

    Recent findings suggest that salerno: I've been pleasantly surprised with the Lakers so far. The pieces are working together nicely. However, the Lakers obviously wouldn't obvousuly be this good without Dončić, who is somehow taking his game to an entirely new level. He's on a mission to win MVP. He's been the best player in the league for the first month of the season. I think this will be the year he finally wins the award.

    Sources indicate that botkin: I actually think Darius Acuff's numbers are actually too good in the sense that voters can't fathom a rookie averaging 26 and 7 without it being some fishy gimmick. It's not a gimmick. He just has total control of an NBA offense, which would make any player's numbers go up, Luka Dončić included. That mentioned, Lendeborg has been better as both a real go-to player on a real team and from a scoring efficiency standpoint. The honeymoon has been heavily interrupted with Stephen Curry's injury as the Warriors look, well, like the Kings. But as of now Lendeborg deserves the award. Long term, I'm really watching Darryn Peterson as Utah's season quickly circles the drain. His numbers are rising quickly, and it may not be long before his development becomes Utah's undisputed top priority.

    Gonzalez: Lendeborg picked a fight with Luka in his very first game as a pro, trash-talked while guarding the Lakers superstar, then said he lost all respect for him afterward. He stepped into the starting lineup and immediately looked like he belonged for an injury-plagued Warriors team that sorely needed his presence. And he was so unnerved by a blowout loss to the Spurs that he chopped off his hair, leaving Steve Kerr to tell the media "apparently that's his response to getting beat by 40, is to go right to the barber." His personality alone wins him the award. The numbers are good, too.

    Sources indicate that kalland: This rookie class has lived up to the hype so far, but right now I have to give the edge to the Warriors rookie sensation. Lendeborg came into the league talking that talk, and while he's put his foot in his mouth here and there, he's largely walked the walk to back it up. What separates him from the likes of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer presently is his combination of productivity and efficiency. But we've already seen that take a dip without Stephen Curry so there is certainly an opportunity for others to make up ground as the Warriors struggle without their top star.

    Recent findings suggest that maloney: Lendeborg has started to fade a bit, and so have the Warriors since Steph Curry went down with an oblique injury, but the No. 11 pick has still done enough to earn the nod ahead of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer. Everyone liked the Lendeborg pick for the Warriors, but no one expected this. He's come in and immediately established himself as their second-best player while doing a little bit of everything. He's second among rookies in scoring, second in rebounding, fifth in assists and tied for fourth in steals, all while shooting 37.2% from 3-point range.

    According to recent reports, quinn: Cameron Boozer is probably trending toward winning. His 3-point shooting is coming around, his interior scoring is progressing, and he does all of the little things everyone promised. Darius Acuff has the biggest numbers, but they're fake. Not fake in the empty calories sense, but fake in that all of the other rookies are being asked to play roles on real basketball teams, whereas Sacramento has elected to devote its entire season to Acuff's development by letting him do basically whatever he wants. If we're simply naming the best rookie thus far this season, though, the answer is obviously Yaxel Lendeborg. Things have gotten harder with Stephen Curry sidelined, but Lendeborg has resuscitated Golden State's postseason ambitions. He's scoring efficiently, shouldering an enormous defensive load and has fit into a system that is notoriously tricky for the wrong kinds of players. Boozer may get there by the end of the season, but for now, this is Yaxel's trophy.

    Recent findings suggest that salerno: In my rookie rankings released earlier this week, I had Yaxel Lendeborg No. 1. However, I would give strong consideration to Acuff because he is being asked to do more than any other rookie in his class. He is putting up elite numbers on a very bad Kings team that would be even worse if he wasn't in the lineup. I don't think you can go wrong with any of the top contenders. Darryn Peterson has also played very well as of late and will end up being in the mix down the stretch.

    In a recent development, botkin: So many good options here. Obviously the Grizzlies, who are probably the correct answer. I certainly didn't foresee Minnesota holding this tightly to the rope without Anthony Edwards. But I'm going with the 76ers, who felt like a team that was going to take a while to figure things out but instead are out to a 13-3 record. There are some qualifiers. A perfect 11-0 mark in clutch games is unsustainable, and they can't keep digging themselves into holes (six comeback wins from at least 10 down). But the bottom line is this is a team that looks like it has played together for far longer than it has. The roles clarified almost immediately. Joel Embiid hasn't gotten hurt yet. There's a mental toughness to this team that I suppose makes sense given the individual players we're talking about, but collectively this thing is way more tied together than I thought possible this early in the season.

    It has been revealed that gonzalez: There weren't many people outside of Los Angeles who predicted the Lakers would be atop the Western Conference a month into the season. There might not have been that many inside Los Angeles either. The skepticism can be forgiven considering the Lakers bid goodbye to arguably the greatest player of all time during the summer, then overhauled a large portion of the roster. In came Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Matisse Thybulle, among others. After the reconstruction, head coach JJ Redick noted that for the first time in his tenure "the pieces actually fit together." That's been the case so far on the offensive end. The Lakers are first in points per game and third in offensive rating. It definitely helps that Luka Dončić is playing some of the best basketball of his career and leading the league in scoring by a wide margin. While Dončić battles Victor Wembanyama for MVP frontrunner status, his Lakers are in a race with the Spurs for the top slot in the West. The former isn't much of a surprise, but the latter certainly is.

    Kalland: Yes, the Grizzlies have faced a very generous schedule through the first month of the season, but even with that context, no one predicted a 12-4 start with Ty Jerome hanging out among the league's leading scorers. Cam Boozer's a strong ROY candidate (and is slowly improving his shooting efficiency) and the Grizzlies just keep finding diamonds in the rough to maintain competitiveness. They've got eight guys averaging 10+ points per game and are top 10 in offensive and defensive rating. Reality may arrive soon, but even so, this hot start has given them a great chance at emerging as a Play-In squad in the West.

    Sources indicate that maloney: The NBA intellegencia was high on the Grizzlies coming into the season, but in the sense that they would surpass their win total projection and make a run at the Play-In Tournament. Instead, they've jumped out to a 12-4 start, which has them in fourth place in the Western Conference and is good for the fifth-best record in the league. They lead the league in offensive rating (121.2) and are third in net rating (+9.9) behind only the Spurs and the Celtics. Even though they've had the easiest schedule in the league thus far, this is still remarkable.

    Quinn: For four games with Anthony Edwards, the Timberwolves looked like the NBA's best offense. Then their best player got hurt ... and they became the NBA's best defense. They're hardly slouching as scorers either. LaMelo Ball's playmaking has facilitated breakout years for Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu. Jonathan Kuminga is making 3s and defending like the Warriors always wanted him to. Minnesota's transition from moodiness to giddiness is palpable whenever they play, and when they get Edwards back, they're going to be terrifying.

    In a recent development, salerno: Here is a wild stat for you: Cameron Boozer has a 159-21 record across games in high school, college and the NBA (during the first month of the season). He is the ultimate winner who elevates his respective teams to greater heights. Between Boozer being firmly in the Rookie of the Year race and Ty Jerome making a case as the Most Improved Player, the Grizzlies have been quite entertaining to watch. Memphis has pushed the right buttons.

    Sources indicate that botkin: I'm probably a little biased on this one. I'm a lifelong Warriors fan and figured they would stink this year, but I allowed myself to get my hopes up with the way the team came out of the gate. I should've known better. As soon as Curry went down, which was probably inevitable, the Warriors turned into one of the worst teams in the league. It's a complete bummer. Hopefully he won't be out too much longer, and the Warriors can pick back up where he left off, but this is just a harsh reminder of how thin the margin is for this team, and it's just not likely to go their way over the long haul. If I was born in Indiana, I would say the same thing about Tyrese Haliburton's injury. Same goes for the Toronto fans with Kawhi only managing two games so far. All the injuries stink. But Curry's has hit the hardest.

    According to recent reports, gonzalez: Moving to the 3-2-1 system was unnecessary.     • Friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball. That important date on the offseason calendar is when clubs must make, or "tender," contract offers for the upcoming season to all their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on the 40-player roster. That's every player who isn't a free agent or isn't presently signed to a multi-year contract. Players who are tendered a contract by that deadline remain with their current organizations. Players who aren't offered a contract become free agents.

    Most such decisions are easy and obvious. Others, however, present difficult calls for the organization because of roster crunches, crowded depth charts, or, more commonly, reluctance to retain a player as his salary rises through the arbitration process. While a number of non-tendered players are likely on their way out of the league, a select few others qualify as at least interesting to other teams and, on occasion, a few will even be coveted to varying degrees.

    All that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire. Let's get to it ….

    According to recent reports, the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil has been injured and ineffective the last two seasons. He missed time with a shoulder concern this past season and also spent time in Triple-A. The Yankees moved him to the bullpen late in the season to see whether he could contribute that way, though Gil was unable to make a strong impression in that role. Now 28, Gil still has another three seasons of team control remaining. Whichever team signs him will be able to keep him through 2029, and that extra control, plus his Rookie of the Year pedigree, will no doubt land Gil with a newly introduced team before Opening Day.

    As a 23-year-old in 2023, the infielder and former first-rounder hit 27 home runs in 119 games and looked like a future cornerstone for the Cardinals. Gorman, however, has gotten steadily worse since then thanks largely to his persistent strikeout challenges. Last season, he wound up back at Triple-A for an extended stretch and didn't fare any better upon being recalled. Long-term, the Cardinals will likely look to hand the third base position to rising power prospect Jesús Báez, who was recently added to the 40-player roster. Gorman can be a plus at third and probably still get by at second, and no doubt some team will take a chance on his power.

    On the downside, Larnach is a defensive minus at the corner outfield spots and probably needs to be a DH, and he's also a platoon bat. On the upside, he's been a steady producer from the left side of the plate. This past season, he put up a .352 OBP and an OPS+ of 120 for Minnesota. For his career, he has an OPS+ of 106 across parts of six MLB seasons. He out-hit his underlying indicators by a bit in 2026, but Larnach is still going to be an appealing part-time bat for some teams.

    Recent findings suggest that the Twins cut bait on a right-hander who's made 139 career starts for them since his 2021 big-league debut. Ober boasts a career OPS+ of 102, but that figure has slid over the last two seasons. What's also slid is Ober's fastball velocity, which may be why he's on this list. In his rookie season, he averaged a fringy 92.4 mph with his four-seamer, but last season that figure was down all the way to 88 mph. That put him in the very bottom percentile among MLB hurlers. The 31-year-old Ober still should draw some interest as a depth piece.

    In a recent development, A platoon extraordinaire, Raley has always hit for power against righties, including 15 home runs in only 290 plate appearances against them in 2026. He's sneaky fast and a very good athlete for his size (6-foot-3 and 235 lbs.), good enough to handle the corner outfield spots competently. Raley also has first base experience and can patrol center field in a pinch. The Mariners cut him loose even though he will remain under team control through 2028.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL's three-game Thanksgiving slate concludes with a blockbuster battle between two perennial playoff teams in the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs. A pair of franchises that have regularly butted heads during the Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes eras clash once again in one of the season's biggest showdowns to date.

    As is often the case when they square off in the regular season, there are significant postseason seeding implications at play in this showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Buffalo stands in control of the AFC's No. 1 seed, while Kansas City is in a tightly contested race with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West crown and the top-four seed that comes with it. Should the Chiefs beat the Bills, not only would they solidify their standing in the division hunt, but they would also then give themselves a clear path to the top overall seed and a first-round bye.

    This game stands among the greatest Thanksgiving matchups in NFL history. The combined 17-3 record between the two teams is the second-best mark by win percentage entering a Thanksgiving game in the last 50 seasons.

    Industry observers note that both sides are also playing their best football of the season heading into the holiday duel. This is just the second game in league history to feature two teams riding three-game win streaks in which all of those victories came by 17 or more points. The only other such instance came in 2007 between Tom Brady's Latest England Patriots and Peyton Manning's Indianapolis Colts. The quarterback face-off in this contest is about as legendary as that one.

    Recent findings suggest that it is difficult to knock Kansas City, because when it wins, it does so in resounding fashion and reveals all the makings of a future Super Bowl winner. But the Chiefs' strength of schedule and results against projected playoff teams do raise questions about whether they can take down the Bills on the road in primetime. The Chiefs have only played three games against opponents with winning records all season and are just 1-2 in those contests. Both losses came on the road. Simply put, they have not shown an ability to win games like the one they are about to walk into.

    At the same time, the Bills defeated each of the three best teams on their schedule thus far. Plus, for whatever reason, Allen has Mahomes' number when they meet in the regular season. Add the defensive revival into the equation, and everything comes up Bills in this matchup. Pick: Bills 38, Chiefs 33.
